doc.title: Virginia Mayhew interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 23, 2022

title: The 'Phantoms' recording after 9/11
summary: Her rubato version of Kenny Barron's 'Phantoms' with Ingrid Jensen was her response to 9/11.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I read something about your compositional reaction to 9/11.
I don’t know that I had one — oh I did, yeah my “Phantoms” album.
It’s an interesting concept to try to capture an event or a really incredibly strong emotion in music.

Well I agree with that. It was really just one tune and it was a tune by Kenny Barron called “Phantoms” and I just felt like I think if we play this rubato — Ingrid Jensen and I were playing a lot together then and we just played this rubato and just — I didn’t say anything to them about it but that’s sort of what I was going for was phantoms, like what happened that day. But I didn’t write a whole project about it and I didn’t really set out to do it, it was just — it just came to me.
